title: Investigate: agent edit near JSONL line 77 has no timeline entry — pre-baseline trim drops the edit's event (baseline-demo)
description: In baseline-demo, the agent message at JSONL line 77 ('added least_valuable(store) ...') has no matching tool-result/edit entry in the timeline, so the JSONL line where the edit occurred can't be navigated to from the timeline. Confirmed mechanism candidate: when pre-baseline reconstruction is declined, seedBaseCommitBeacon (jfred/src/reconstruction_base_commit.ts:132) drops every FileEvent at-or-before the beacon insertion point ('dropped N superseded pre-baseline event(s)') — the edit's WriteEvent never survives, so no revision, no fileChanges chip, no timeline entry; the git-derived baseline synthetic turn (recordGitBaselineSnapshot, jfred/webapp/views/timeline-nodes.ts:69) absorbs only the gitBase snapshot, it does not literally merge the edit. Verify against the baseline-demo session (was preBaseline declined? does the entry appear when accepted?), then decide the fix: even when trimmed, the turn should probably still be navigable to its JSONL line even if its file event is superseded.

title: Paths... popover -> settings WIZARD: design the flow (mockup first), then implement
description:
DIRECTION CHANGE 2026-07-21 (supersedes the earlier two-section-popover mockup): the Paths... popover should become a settings WIZARD:
- screen 1: set the project path
- screen 2: 'do you wish to set a custom file history snapshot path or auto-derive the path?'
- screen 3: 'do you wish to set a Git Repo path?'
- screen 4: 'do you wish to pick a git repo commit? (default: master branch tip)'
DELIVERABLE ORDER: (a) define the wizard's flow logic via UI/UX MOCKUP first, (b) define how values are CHANGED for a session after it loads (re-enter the wizard? jump to a single screen? a compact summary panel with per-row edit?), (c) only then implement. The user says ambiguities must be flushed out first — resolve these in the mockup step:
(1) TRIGGER: when does the wizard run — first launch with no config? every folder switch? on demand from the Paths... button? (screen 1 is GLOBAL config, screens 2-4 are effectively per-project — reveng-paths.json entries — so does the wizard rerun per project?)
(2) Screen-2 default: auto-derive (today's behavior — empty posts '' and the server re-derives, app-header.ts computeFileHistoryDirToPost).
(3) Screen-4 default 'master branch tip': which ref when the repo's default branch isn't master, and should the default instead be the commit the SESSION records (the s85-style recorded baseline) when one exists?
(4) Skip semantics: declining screens 3/4 must leave the project reconstructing exactly as with no reveng-paths entry.
(5) Persistence: where each screen's answer lands (screen 1 -> /api/config global; screens 2-4 -> /api/project-paths, persist flag) and whether the wizard's finish step is the 137-style 'store?' prompt.
(6) The task-56 pre-baseline question ('reconstruct file states preceding the baseline commit?') fires at project load — decide whether it becomes a wizard screen or stays a load-time dialog.
CARRY-OVERS still wanted from the pre-wizard design: picker-button naming 'Set Projects Folder location' / 'Set Git Repo location'; Store subsumes Apply (postProjectPaths(true) applies AND persists, app-paths-project.ts:122-123); commit pick list = task 154's 500-newest list (search box open there). Existing code sites: #paths-popover jfred/webapp/index.html:17-40, app-header.ts, app-paths-project.ts, /api/project-paths route.

title: 'constructing branches' progress: show an incrementing record counter, not just the static graphic
description: The 'constructing branches' stage shows only the stage label/graphic on the progress bar; the user wants visible forward motion — a counter that increments as records are processed (which record k of N is being handled). Mechanism today: buildProjectReconstruction (jfred/src/viewer_api.ts:65) emits the single stage label PROGRESS_LABEL_CONSTRUCTING_BRANCHES (viewer_api.ts:38, listed in webapp/app-progress.ts:38), then reconstructBranches (jfred/src/reconstruction_engine.ts:212) runs silently: findConversationBranches walks all records, reconstructAll covers the surviving branch (its per-target 'reconstructing <target> n/N' counter exists — task 149 family), and each rewound branch goes through buildRewoundBranchHistory with NO progress emission at all. Fix: thread the existing deep-engine progress channel (reportReconstructionProgress — it already reaches the UI progress line) into the silent parts: a records-walked counter for the branch enumeration ('scanning records k/N') and a per-branch counter for the rewound pass ('rewound branch k of n — <m> records'). Counter granularity: update every ~100 records, not every record — the sink funnels into DOM text and per-record updates would throttle the build it's reporting on.

title: Progress overlay: scope it to the timeline pane (console stays usable) + Cancel-with-confirm back to project picker
description:
The loading-progress popup currently overlays the whole GUI including the console (the cancel/copy/hide-console buttons remain interactive underneath, but visually everything is covered). Change: attach the progress box to the TIMELINE AREA only, so only the timeline is blocked while the rest of the GUI stays enabled. Mechanism: buildLoadingProgressElements creates .timeline-progress-overlay and appends it to document.body (jfred/webapp/app-progress.ts:79 and :102) — reparent it into the timeline pane (#timeline-pane / #view) with position:absolute over that pane instead of a body-level overlay; adjust .timeline-progress-overlay in webapp/styles.css accordingly.
CANCEL: add a 'Cancel' button ON the progress box that stops reconstruction mid-stream. Abort machinery exists — inflightLoadController (app-fetch.ts:104), already wired to the console's #console-cancel button (index.html:92) and to navigation teardown (app-router.ts:60). Flow: click Cancel -> ask the user to confirm ('cancel this reconstruction?') -> on yes, abort the controller and navigate to the pick-project screen (location.hash = '#/'). Confirm must be an in-DOM dialog, NOT window.confirm — the codebase convention bans native dialogs because they block headless automation (comment at app-header.ts folder-switch handler). Note the navigation to '#/' itself aborts the in-flight load, so 'yes' can simply be: location.hash = '#/' (+ renderRoute if already on #/) — one code path, no separate abort call needed. Also decide whether #console-cancel stays or is retired in favor of the progress-box Cancel (one cancel affordance is enough).

title: Phase-4 blowup: nested lineage replays re-run the full per-target pipeline once per (target, timestamp)
description: ROOT CAUSE of the task-156 stall (2252s+ observed on the 451-target RevEng project, 2026-07-21; task 150's garbage-target fix addressed a different symptom). Evidence from jfred-server.log (70s window): 473 'replaying lineage of' headers over only 140 distinct targets — one target replayed 27x, another 56x (sic, from the script-stage tally); plans/items29-30-31-32-close.md replayed 3x in 47s. Mechanism: replayLineageContentBefore (src/reconstruction_branches.ts:199) replays a target's ENTIRE reconstruction pipeline once per (target, before-timestamp) cycleKey, and each replay re-runs every stage including injectScriptExecutions over ALL 1447 discovered runs ('script stage: 1447 runs for <target>' x473). The lineageSeedsByKey memo only caches replays entered on a CLEAN seeding stack (enteredWithCleanStack, lines 207-225) — nested replays recompute fresh every time and are never cached. Also observed: placeGitCommitEvidence is the slowest per-replay stage (0.16-0.37s each; the logged run's last line sat there). Fix directions to evaluate in planning: (a) safely memoize nested replays (the current guard exists because a nested replay's result can be degraded by outer cycle guards — cache only proven-undegraded results, or key the cache by the active seeding stack); (b) compute a target's full revision list ONCE and slice per `before` — CAUTION: enterLineageReplayWindow(before) sets a time cutoff that changes reconstruction (the s87 time-aware indirection), so slicing is only valid where the cutoff provably doesn't alter the prefix; (c) hoist the 1447-run script-run discovery/filtering out of the per-replay path. Reproduce: load project -Users-matkatmusicllc-Desktop-claude-code-src-RevEng with script consent, pipe server stdout to a log, count 'replaying lineage of' repeats per target.
